name: Xavier Becerra
role: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2021–2025); California Democratic nominee for governor (2026)
summary: Becerra is a Democrat who spent 24 years in the U.S. House, then served as California attorney general and Biden's health secretary. His record is progressive on health care, abortion, LGBT rights, immigration and the environment, with a cautious record on trade and a mixed one on policing and the death penalty.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted Nay on the Hyde amendments (c103#295, #297) and on the partial-birth abortion ban (c104#960); as attorney general he litigated to protect abortion access.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He says California cannot accept technology moving so fast that workers' livelihoods and children's safety are left behind.

algorithmic-government.rationale: He wants human review of high-stakes automated decisions and guardrails on AI operating beyond human oversight.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Voted Yea in 2014 on authorizing training and equipping vetted Syrian opposition forces (clerk roll 507; c113).

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted Yea on the 2008 Economic Stimulus Act (c110#1201, #1218).

ban-cartels.rationale: As attorney general he brought an antitrust suit against a hospital system and joined multistate antitrust actions.

build-apartments-freely.rationale: His housing platform says most California residential land excludes apartments and pledges zoning reform, by-right approvals near jobs and transit, and an end to exclusionary zoning around more transit.

death-penalty.rationale: Voted Nay on the 1995 Effective Death Penalty Act (c104#104) but Yea on the 1994 crime bill that expanded federal capital offenses (c103#1005); as attorney general he defended death sentences while pledging to extend the moratorium.

dense-cities.rationale: His housing platform backs transit-oriented housing because it reduces carbon emissions.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted Yea on the American Clean Energy and Security Act (c111#475) and the 2007 CLEAN Energy Act (c110#39); as attorney general he defended clean-car rules.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Voted Yea on ENDA (c110#1050) and DADT repeal (c111#1621), and as attorney general brought civil-rights enforcement actions.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted Nay on ANWR drilling (c107#318) and the 2005 energy acts (c109#131), and as attorney general sued over federal drilling.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted Nay on the balanced-budget amendment (c104#47) but Yea on the 1994 Budget Control Act setting spending targets (c103#939).

free-trade.rationale: Voted Yea on NAFTA (c103#558) and China PNTR (c106#835) but Nay on CAFTA (c109#442) and the Colombia agreement (c112#777).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voted Yea on the Employment Non-Discrimination Act (c110#1050), and as attorney general defended state anti-discrimination law.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He introduced legislation in 2003 to expand the earned income tax credit for lower-income working parents and individuals.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Voted Yea on the Campaign Reform Act of 1993 with spending and contribution limits (c103#587).

limit-guns.rationale: Voted Yea on the Brady Act (c103#548) and the 1994 assault-weapons ban (c103#750) and, as attorney general, sued over ghost-gun frames.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Voted Yea on mandatory minimum sentences for gun crimes (c105#649) and the 1994 crime bill conference report (c103#1005).

minority-language-support.rationale: He voted Nay on the amendment to prohibit bilingual voting materials (c105#987) and Nay on making English the official government language (c104#1257).

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted Nay on the 2001 airline bailout (c107#345) and TARP (c110#1856) but Yea on the 2008 auto rescue (c110#1865).

open-borders.rationale: At the 2026 debate he said "it is good to have a regulated system of immigrants" and for regulation of the border.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Voted Nay on codifying Don't Ask, Don't Tell (c103#447, #456) and Yea on its repeal (c111#1621).

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: As HHS Secretary he condemned state restrictions on gender-affirming care for trans youth as an attack on bodily autonomy that strips parents of decisions and interferes with doctors' judgment.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He voted Yea on the Electronic Freedom of Information Amendments Act of 1996 (c104#1280) and the Freedom of Information Act Amendments of 2007 (c110#143).

public-service-media.rationale: He voted against cutting Corporation for Public Broadcasting funding (Nay on the Hefley cut c103#293, the Crane rescission c104#238 and the Crane elimination c105#384) and for adding public broadcasting facilities funds (Yea on the Engel amendment c104#567).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted Yea on the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007 (c110#17) and for the 2000 minimum-wage increase (c106#650-651).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Voted Yea on limiting aid to Turkey until it acknowledges the Armenian genocide (c104#1083) and on the Darfur genocide resolution (c108#1094).

reduce-immigration.rationale: Voted Nay on H.R. 4437 (c109#659), the Secure Fence Act (c109#1114) and the 1996 Immigration Act (c104#955); as attorney general he sued over restrictive federal immigration policies.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Voted Yea on the Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (c111#966), and as attorney general brought antitrust and consumer enforcement against large companies.

rehabilitation.rationale: Voted Yea on the Second Chance Act of 2007 (c110#1076) and alternative punishment for youth offenders (c103#573).

rent-control.rationale: His housing platform pledges to enforce the Tenant Protection Act's limits on excessive rent increases.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted Yea on the Cesar Chavez Workplace Fairness Act (c103#215), which barred permanent replacement of strikers.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted Nay on the D.C. Student Opportunity Scholarship Act (c105#747) and the HELP Scholarships Amendments (c105#563).

single-official-language.rationale: Voted Nay on making English the official language (c104#1257) and Nay on banning bilingual ballots (c105#987), but Yea on English requirements for Puerto Rico statehood (c105#661).

state-directs-investment.rationale: His film-industry platform would use state tax credits and financing to build up a strategic industry.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He introduced the LEND Act to forgive student loans for librarians in critical-need areas, and as attorney general he urged the Education Department to discharge the loans of tens of thousands of disabled veterans.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted Yea on the 2001 PATRIOT Act (c107#394) and the 2015 USA FREEDOM Act (c114#223) but Nay on the 2008 FISA Amendments Act (c110#1612).

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted Nay on the Permanent Estate Tax Relief Act of 2006 (c109#983).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted Nay on the 2001 Bush tax cuts (c107#117) and the 2003 Jobs and Growth tax cut (c108#181).

term-limits.rationale: Voted Nay on the term-limits constitutional amendments of 1995 (c104#269) and 1997 (c105#20).

unions-good.rationale: Voted Yea on the Cesar Chavez Workplace Fairness Act (c103#215) and the Employee Free Choice Act (c110#117).

universal-healthcare.rationale: He says California is "moving towards universal coverage for all Californians who work hard" and that single payer ("Medicare for all") would be the most efficient system; his platform says to build toward universal access.

voter-id.rationale: Voted Nay on the Federal Election Integrity Act of 2006 (c109#1127); as attorney general he fought voter-ID laws.
